# IVR prompt sheet: debt inquiry and statement week change

Burcu Tan, IVR operations, 10 Sep 2026

Selin asked for "whatever the menu says today" before the kickoff, so here it is. I copied these out of the prompt list in our IVR designer this morning, card self-service branch, debt inquiry and statement week nodes only. Variable names are the ones the TTS template uses, not the service fields. Amounts and dates go through the number-to-speech module; everything else is recorded or plain TTS.

I haven't cleaned it up much. Some of these were written years ago and nobody has touched them since, so please don't read them as "how it should be". Questions to me, wording questions to Kerem.

## Debt inquiry

| Prompt id | When it plays | Turkish line | Variables |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBT-010 | Card has no unpaid statement debt | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınızda ödenmemiş bir borç görünmüyor. Bir sonraki ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| DBT-020 | Opening of the debt reading, before the per-currency lines | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız için bilgiler şöyle: | last4, card_name |
| DBT-031 | TL debt, caller has paid nothing yet | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası; yapmanız gereken en düşük ödeme {tl_min} Türk Lirası. | tl_total, tl_min |
| DBT-032 | TL debt, caller paid the minimum or more | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası, geriye kalan borcunuz {tl_remaining} Türk Lirası. Asgari ödemenizi yaptınız, teşekkür ederiz. | tl_total, tl_remaining |
| DBT-033 | TL debt, caller paid something but less than the minimum | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası, yapmanız gereken en düşük ödeme {tl_min} Türk Lirası. Geriye kalan borcunuz {tl_remaining} Türk Lirası, ödemeniz gereken kalan asgari tutar ise {tl_remaining_min} Türk Lirası. | tl_total, tl_min, tl_remaining, tl_remaining_min |
| DBT-040 | Dollar debt (own sentence, plays after the TL line) | Dolar cinsinden toplam borcunuz {usd_total} USD, geriye kalan borcunuz {usd_remaining} USD, en düşük ödeme tutarı {usd_min} USD. | usd_total, usd_remaining, usd_min |
| DBT-041 | Euro debt (own sentence, plays after the dollar line) | Euro cinsinden toplam borcunuz {eur_total} Euro, geriye kalan borcunuz {eur_remaining} Euro, en düşük ödeme tutarı {eur_min} Euro. | eur_total, eur_remaining, eur_min |
| DBT-051 | No debt in TL | Türk Lirası cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-052 | No debt in dollar | Dolar cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-053 | No debt in euro | Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-054 | No debt in TL and dollar | Türk Lirası ve Dolar cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-055 | No debt in TL and euro | Türk Lirası ve Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-056 | No debt in dollar and euro | Dolar ve Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-060 | After the currency lines | Tüm borçlarınız için son ödeme gününüz {due_date}. | due_date |
| DBT-071 | After the debt info, debt or no debt: overall TL total | Bekleyen provizyonlar, faiz ve masraflar hesaba katılmadan kartınızın toplam Türk Lirası borcu {tl_overall} Türk Lirası. | tl_overall |
| DBT-072 | Same, overall dollar total | Bekleyen provizyonlar, faiz ve masraflar hesaba katılmadan toplam dolar borcu {usd_overall} dolar. | usd_overall |

Ops notes, debt inquiry:
- The three TL lines are picked by the IVR from the paid amount vs. the minimum. Ask Mert for the exact comparison, I only know it works.
- Dollar and euro are separate prompts on purpose; the recording studio would not do one sentence with two slots. "USD" is read out by the TTS as written. Yes, people have complained.
- There is no Sterling prompt at all. Never came up on the menu.
- The script I was handed in 2023 had the dollar total line (DBT-072) written twice and no euro total line. We recorded it once. So no euro total plays today.
- DBT-051 to DBT-056 cover only six combinations. If a card has no debt in any currency it goes to DBT-010 and never reaches these.

## Statement week change

| Prompt id | When it plays | Turkish line | Variables |

Önümüzdeki dönemde ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, linked_card_name, week_ordinal, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| STW-012 | Current payment week, the linked card itself (caller holds the card that hangs off a main card) | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız ile bu kartın bağlı olduğu {main_card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına ayarlı. Önümüzdeki dönemde ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, main_card_name, week_ordinal, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| STW-020 | Caller picked a week; IVR reads what the change will mean (after statement.week.decide) | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alınacak. Bundan sonra ekstreniz {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | last4, card_name, week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-021 | Same, card with a linked card | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız ile buna bağlı {linked_card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alınacak. Bundan sonra ekstreniz {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | last4, card_name, linked_card_name, week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-030 | Right after STW-020 / STW-021 | Bu değişikliği onaylar mısınız? | none |
| STW-040 | Caller confirmed and statement.week.change succeeded | Onayınızla ödeme gününüz her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alındı. Ekstreniz artık {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-091 | statement.week.change refuses: already changed this month | Ekstre tarihinizi değiştiremedik. Ekstre tarihi ayda yalnızca bir kez değiştirilebiliyor. | none |
| STW-092 | statement.week.change refuses: yearly limit reached | Ekstre tarihinizi değiştiremedik. Ekstre tarihi yılda en çok üç kez değiştirilebiliyor. | none |
| STW-099 | statement.week.change errors or times out | Şu an sisteme ulaşamıyoruz, ekstre tarihiniz değişmedi. Birkaç dakika sonra tekrar arayabilirsiniz. | none |

Ops notes, statement week:
- week_ordinal is a word ("birinci", "ikinci" ...), not a number. The TTS says "1." badly.
- There is no linked-card variant of STW-020 for the case where the caller holds the linked card. It falls back to STW-021 with the names swapped, which sounds slightly off. Known.
- STW-091 and STW-092 only play after the caller has already confirmed, because we only find out from the change call. Callers find that annoying ("why did you ask me then"). I don't know of a way to check before; maybe Mert does.
- The limits in STW-091/092 are what the card system answered when these were recorded. I have not checked them against the product side recently, Kerem would know.

182

184	{{account_facts}}
185	
186	{{date_facts}}

188	{{date_answers}}

191	1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it is paid/dispute/hardship).
192	2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "Do you confirm?" and WAIT for the customer's answer.
193	3. Only after a clear yes: create_promise, one per agreed product.
194	4. add_note for each product without a promise.
195	5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
196	NEVER call create_promise in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do step 2 and wait.
197	Example: "I'll pay the card tomorrow, not the other two" = card agreed for tomorrow (check DATE ANSWERS); then the second product: make its attempt 1; if refused and it has attempt 2, make attempt 2; then the third product the same way; only then step 2.
198	
199	HOW TO NEGOTIATE
200	- The question about paying today is asked ONCE for all products (already asked). If yes for all: the promise is the full amount of every product dated today.
201	- If not all today: go through the products one by one in the order above. For each product start at its attempt 1. Never ask about today again.
202	- Always ask for the full past-due amount first. NEVER ask "how much can you pay?" - you propose every amount.
203	- Customer names a date: use DATE ANSWERS. A vague period ("next week", "end of month", "when my salary comes"): ask once for the exact day; a named day then goes through DATE ANSWERS; if still none, propose that product's deadline.
204	- "Next <weekday>" = that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" = in the current week.
205	- If the customer names ONE date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, that product gets its own deadline and the others keep the named date; say so in the read-back.
206	- Full amount too much: offer the product's floor once and say the rest stays overdue. Amount from floor to full (inclusive): accept. Below floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
207	- A proposed date or amount is never a refusal.
208	- Flat refusal, non-answer, refusing the floor, refusing the deadline offer: that uses one persuasion attempt for that product. Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer): that product is refused. When several products are refused in one sentence, still go through them one at a time with their attempts.
209	- Illness, death in the family or job loss: one short sentence of sympathy, NO persuasion; offer to connect them with the customer support team. Accept: transfer_to_agent queue support, close transferred / support. Decline: the remaining unpromised products get note hardship. If they still name a date or amount themselves, handle it normally.
210	- "I already paid" (this past-due amount) for a product: say payments can take one business day to appear; no promise for it; it gets note paid; continue with the other products.
211	- "Not mine" / "never had it" / "closed or paid off in the past": do not argue; no promise; note dispute; continue with the others.
212	- New payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Do NOT record any agreed-but-unrecorded promise. Call transfer_to_agent queue restructuring, close transferred / restructuring.
213	- On ANY transfer never call add_note, before or after it.
214	- Customer says twice they do not want to talk: remaining products get note refused, then close.
215	- Recorded promises cannot be changed or cancelled; they can change it in the mobile app.
216	
217	READ-BACK AND RECORDING
218	- When every product is settled (promise agreed or no promise), read ALL agreed promises back together in ONE message in future tense: "To confirm: <product> <amount> on <weekday day month>; <next product> ... Do you confirm?" Do not use the words recorded, booked, saved, registered, set up or done before create_promise returned ok.
219	- If they change a date or amount, check it again and read everything back again.
220	- After a clear yes: call create_promise once per agreed product (product_id, amount as a number, date YYYY-MM-DD), one at a time, in order. Follow what_to_do_next.
221	- Then for EACH product without a recorded promise call add_note with its product_id and reason (refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error). Also when no product has a promise.
222	
223	CLOSING (thank and say goodbye in the same turn as close_call)
224	- At least one promise recorded and no transfer: outcome promise.
225	- Transfer happened: outcome transferred with that transfer's reason.
226	- No promise recorded: if every product is noted paid, outcome paid; otherwise outcome no_promise with the reason of the FIRST product in account order whose note is not paid."""
227	
228	WF = {
229	    "initial_node": "setup",
230	    "system_prompt": SYSTEM,
231	    "test_variables": {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Dana", "last_name": "Fisher", "title": "Ms", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"},
232	    "nodes": {},
233	}
234	N = WF["nodes"]
235	N["setup"] = code_node("setup", SETUP_CODE, "greet")
236	
237	N["greet"] = {
238	    "name": "greet", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": OPENING}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
239	    "task_message": GREET_TASK,
240	    "extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
241	                           "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "wrong_number", "unclear"],
242	                           "description": "Who answered. customer ONLY if the person said yes, that's me, speaking, or the customer's own name. someone_else if the person says they are someone else (a relative, colleague, etc.) or the customer is not available. wrong_number if the number does not belong to the customer. Otherwise unclear (hello, go ahead, who is this, questions)."}],
243	    "tools": [close_tool(["not_reached", "not_verified", "transferred"], ["unclear", "wrong_number", "deceased", "declined", "human"],
244	                         "not_reached/unclear: still unclear after the second ask. not_reached/wrong_number: not the customer's number. not_reached/deceased: customer has died. not_verified/declined: refuses to talk twice. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
245	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
246	    "transitions": [END_T,
247	                    {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
248	                    {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}],
249	}
250	
251	N["third_party"] = {
252	    "name": "third_party", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
253	    "task_message": THIRD_TASK,
254	    "tools": [api_tool("schedule_callback", "Book a callback. CALL it only when the person gave a day and time inside the allowed callback slots.",
255	                       {"date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_date}}", "description": "Callback date YYYY-MM-DD, today or the next business day only."},
256	                        "time": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_time}}", "description": "Callback time HH:MM, 24h, from 10:00 to 19:00."}},
257	                       ["date", "time"], retries=0, post=CALLBACK_POST),
258	              close_tool(["not_reached", "transferred"], ["callback", "no_callback", "wrong_number", "deceased", "human"],
259	                         "not_reached/callback: callback booked. not_reached/no_callback: no valid time after one re-ask. not_reached/wrong_number. not_reached/deceased. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
260	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
261	    "transitions": [END_T],
262	}
263	
264	N["identity"] = {
265	    "name": "identity", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
266	    "task_message": IDENTITY_TASK,
267	    "tools": [api_tool("verify_identity", "Check one security answer. CALL it every time the customer answers a security question.",
268	                       {"field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["date_of_birth", "phone_last4"], "default": "{{field}}", "description": "date_of_birth for the first question, phone_last4 for the second."},
269	                        "answer": {"type": "string", "default": "{{answer}}", "description": "date_of_birth as YYYY-MM-DD (numbers only: day, month, year); phone_last4 as four digits."}},
270	                       ["field", "answer"], retries=1, post=VERIFY_POST),
271	              close_tool(["not_verified", "transferred"], ["failed", "declined", "human"],
272	                         "not_verified/failed: three wrong answers. not_verified/declined: refused the questions twice (or asked what the call is about twice). transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
273	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the customer insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],

275	                    {"target_node": "fetch_account", "description": "identity verified", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
276	                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
277	                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}],

281	N["fetch_account"] = {"name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": "account",
282	                      "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "pre_actions": [fetch],

288	    "name": "collect", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
289	    "task_message": COLLECT_TASK,
290	    "tools": [api_tool("create_promise", "Record one payment promise for one product. CALL it only after the customer said a clear yes to the full read-back, once per agreed product.",
291	                       {"product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "product_id from the account facts"},
292	                        "amount": {"type": "number", "default": "{{amount}}", "description": "Agreed amount, a number, from the floor up to the full past-due amount."},
293	                        "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "Agreed date YYYY-MM-DD, a business day, today or later, not after the product's deadline."}},
294	                       ["product_id", "amount", "date"], retries=0, post=PROMISE_POST),
295	              api_tool("add_note", "Record why one product ended without a promise. CALL it once per product without a recorded promise, after the promises are recorded. NEVER call it when a transfer happened or will happen.",

298	                       ["product_id", "reason"], retries=0, post=NOTE_POST),

# EXAMPLE ONLY: the build script that passed every practice customer of the kit's Brief A + B
# (4 separate runs: plain speech, answers in pieces, self-corrections, 3 repetitions).
#
# Use it for the SHAPE: the node graph (setup -> greet -> third_party | identity -> fetch_account
# -> account -> collect -> end), entry types, the hook() helper, the per-node close_call enums,
# and the STRICT ORDER block in COLLECT_TASK. Recording happens in collect itself.
#
# Every sentence, value, word list, outcome, reason and rule below belongs to that one brief.
# Do NOT copy any of it into another brief's agent. Write yours from your own spec.
#

import json, subprocess, sys, os

SKILL = ".claude/skills/build-phone-agent"
SERVER = "https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev/v1"


def code_of(snippet, out):
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", snippet, "--out", out], check=True)
    return open(out, encoding="utf-8").read()


SETUP_CODE = code_of("out/brief-b_setup_snippet.py", "out/brief-b_setup_code.txt")
ACCOUNT_CODE = code_of("out/brief-b_account_snippet.py", "out/brief-b_account_code.txt")


def code_node(name, code, target):
    return {"name": name, "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": target,
            "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
            "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
                    "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
            "transitions": [{"target_node": target, "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]}


def api_tool(name, desc, body_props, required, retries=0, post="", pre="", timeout=12000):
    props = {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}", "description": "The customer id."}}
    props.update(body_props)
    t = {"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": timeout, "maxRetries": retries},
         "function": {"name": name, "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": desc,
                      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                          "url": {"type": "string", "default": SERVER + "/" + name},
                          "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
                          "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
                          "body": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required}}}}}
    if post:
        t["post_process_code"] = post
    if pre:
        t["pre_process_code"] = pre
    return t


def hook(body):
    lines = ["try:", "    if isinstance(result, dict):", "        result.pop('header', None)",
             "        d = result.get('data')", "        if not isinstance(d, dict):", "            d = dict()",
             "            result['data'] = d",
             "        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400",
             "        err = str(d.get('error') or result.get('message') or '').lower()"]
    lines += ["        " + l for l in body.strip("\n").split("\n")]
    lines += ["except Exception:", "    pass", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


VERIFY_POST = hook("""
left = d.get('wrong_answers_left')
if d.get('all_verified') is True or str(d.get('all_verified')) in ('true', 'True'):
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'IDENTITY VERIFIED. Say only: Thank you, that is confirmed. Nothing else.'
elif d.get('hint') == 'day_month_swapped':
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Not counted as wrong. Ask the customer to say their date of birth again with the month as a word, for example the 3rd of June 1987.'
elif not ok and d.get('verified') is None:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The answer could not be read and was NOT counted. Ask the same question again; for a date ask for day, month as a word, and year.'
elif d.get('verified') is True:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Correct. Now ask the second question: the last four digits of the phone number on file.'
elif left is not None and int(left) <= 0:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'CHECK FAILED, no tries left. Do not mention any account, amount or reason for the call. Say they can use the Freya Bank mobile app or visit a branch, thank them, say goodbye, and call close_call with outcome not_verified and reason failed.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Wrong answer. Ask the SAME question once more, without saying what is on file.'
""")

PROMISE_POST = hook("""
if ok or 'already' in err or 'exists' in err:
    d['ok'] = True
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED for this product_id. Never call create_promise again for this product. If another agreed promise from the read-back is not recorded yet, call create_promise for it now. When all are recorded, say exactly: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." Then, for any product without a promise, call add_note; then close.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. If this was the FIRST try for this product, call create_promise again now with exactly the same values. If it was the SECOND failed try, say you could not record the promise for this product, call add_note for it with reason service_error, then continue with the other products.'
""")

NOTE_POST = hook("""
if ok or 'already' in err or 'exists' in err:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Note saved. Never note this product again. Continue with the next product in order; if every product is handled, give the closing words and call close_call per the closing rule.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The note failed. Call add_note once more with the same values.'
""")

TRANSFER_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'TRANSFERRED. Do NOT call add_note or create_promise. Say thank you and goodbye, then call close_call with outcome transferred and reason restructuring (queue restructuring), human (queue general) or support (queue support).'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The transfer failed. Call transfer_to_agent once more with the same queue.'
""")

CALLBACK_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Callback booked. Thank them, say goodbye, call close_call with outcome not_reached and reason callback.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT booked. Call schedule_callback once more with the same values. If it fails again, say it could not be booked, thank them and close with not_reached and reason no_callback.'
""")

CLOSE_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The call is closed. Say nothing more.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'close_call failed. Call close_call once more with the same values.'
""")

CLOSE_PRE = """try:
    b = config.get('body')
    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('promise', 'paid'):
        b.pop('reason', None)
except Exception:
    pass
"""


def close_tool(outcomes, reasons, desc):
    props = {"outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": outcomes, "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": desc},
             "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": reasons, "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "The reason that goes with the outcome. Leave empty for promise and paid."}}
    return api_tool("close_call", "End the call. CALL it exactly once, as the very last tool call, in the same turn as your thank-you and goodbye. " + desc,
                    props, ["outcome"], retries=0, post=CLOSE_POST, pre=CLOSE_PRE)


def transfer_tool(queues, desc):
    return api_tool("transfer_to_agent", desc, {"queue": {"type": "string", "enum": queues, "default": "{{queue}}", "description": "restructuring = new payment plan or lower instalments; general = the customer insists on a human; support = hardship and accepted support."}},
                    ["queue"], retries=0, post=TRANSFER_POST)


END_T = {"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
    {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
    {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}

FORBID = 'Before identity is verified NEVER say any of these words or hint at them: "collections", "debt", "payment", "owe", "late", "overdue", "account", "loan", "credit card", "product". If asked what the call is about, say only that it is a personal matter for {{title}} {{last_name}}.'

SYSTEM = """You are Freya Bank's digital assistant on an outbound phone call. Speak English. Be brief and polite: one or two short sentences per turn, ONE question per turn.
After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end a turn with nothing said. Call one tool at a time.
Address the customer as {{title}} {{last_name}}.
If asked whether you are a robot or an AI: say you are Freya Bank's digital assistant, then continue with your current question.
If asked whether this is a scam: say they can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, then continue with your current question.
If the person asks for a human: the first time ask whether you can help them first. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent with queue general, then close as transferred with reason human.
A question you cannot answer from your facts or tools: say you do not have that information. Never invent figures, dates or reasons.
Never claim an action happened unless its tool returned ok. Never offer a discount, waiver, instalment plan or any other term.
Before close_call always thank the customer and say goodbye, in the same turn as the close_call call. close_call is always the last tool call."""

OPENING = "Hello, this is Freya Bank's digital assistant calling. This call is recorded. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?"

GREET_TASK = FORBID + """
You asked whether you are speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}. No tool call except close_call and transfer_to_agent is allowed here.
- Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead", "who is this" do NOT.
- If it is not a confirmation (or they asked a question; answer it first per the rules), ask again exactly: "Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?" This is your second and last ask. If still unclear after the second ask: thank them, say goodbye, call close_call with outcome not_reached, reason unclear.
- If they say this number does not belong to that person: apologise, say goodbye, close_call not_reached / wrong_number.
- If they say the customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." Ask nothing else, say goodbye, close_call not_reached / deceased.
- If the person refuses to talk twice: thank them, goodbye, close_call not_verified / declined."""

THIRD_TASK = FORBID + """
Someone other than {{title}} {{last_name}} is on the line. Do not say why you are calling. Do not answer any question about the customer or any money matter, even if they offer to pay; say only that it is a personal matter. Ask when {{title}} {{last_name}} can be reached.
{{callback_facts}}
- If they name a day and time inside the allowed slots: call schedule_callback with date YYYY-MM-DD and time HH:MM (24h). Then thank, goodbye, close_call not_reached / callback.
- If the day or time is outside the slots: ask ONCE for another time, naming the allowed window (today or the next business day, between 10:00 and 19:00). If the second answer is also outside, do not schedule: thank, goodbye, close_call not_reached / no_callback. Also no_callback if they give no time.
- If they say the number does not belong to the customer: close_call not_reached / wrong_number.
- If they say the customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, goodbye, close_call not_reached / deceased."""

IDENTITY_TASK = FORBID + """
The customer confirmed who they are. Check identity with two security questions, one at a time.
1. Say that for security you need to ask two questions, and ask for their date of birth. When they answer, call verify_identity with field date_of_birth and answer as YYYY-MM-DD. A date given only as numbers is day, then month, then year (03/06/1987 = 1987-06-03). Convert spoken dates yourself.
2. Then ask for the last four digits of the phone number on file and call verify_identity with field phone_last4 and the four digits.
Follow what_to_do_next after each result. Never reveal what is on file.
- Customers often give an answer in PIECES over several turns ("nineteen October" then "nineteen eighty three"; "forty four" then "ten" = 4410). Combine the pieces of the current answer. If the answer is not complete yet, reply only "Yes, go on." (do NOT repeat the question). As soon as you have a full date or four digits, call verify_identity.
- If they do not want to answer, or ask what the call is about instead of answering: explain ONCE that the questions protect their account and ask again. If they refuse again or ask again: thank, goodbye, close_call not_verified / declined.
- A request for a human follows the system rule (transfer queue general, close transferred / human)."""

COLLECT_TASK = """Identity is verified. You have already said this aloud: "{{debt_statement}}"

ACCOUNT FACTS (one line per product, in order):
{{account_facts}}

{{date_facts}}
DATE ANSWERS: when the customer names a day, find it here and do exactly what its line says for each product:
{{date_answers}}

STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it is paid/dispute/hardship).
2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "Do you confirm?" and WAIT for the customer's answer.
3. Only after a clear yes: create_promise, one per agreed product.
4. add_note for each product without a promise.
5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
NEVER call create_promise in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do step 2 and wait.
Example: "I'll pay the card tomorrow, not the other two" = card agreed for tomorrow (check DATE ANSWERS); then the second product: make its attempt 1; if refused and it has attempt 2, make attempt 2; then the third product the same way; only then step 2.

HOW TO NEGOTIATE
- The question about paying today is asked ONCE for all products (already asked). If yes for all: the promise is the full amount of every product dated today.
- If not all today: go through the products one by one in the order above. For each product start at its attempt 1. Never ask about today again.
- Always ask for the full past-due amount first. NEVER ask "how much can you pay?" - you propose every amount.
- Customer names a date: use DATE ANSWERS. A vague period ("next week", "end of month", "when my salary comes"): ask once for the exact day; a named day then goes through DATE ANSWERS; if still none, propose that product's deadline.
- "Next <weekday>" = that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" = in the current week.
- If the customer names ONE date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, that product gets its own deadline and the others keep the named date; say so in the read-back.
- Full amount too much: offer the product's floor once and say the rest stays overdue. Amount from floor to full (inclusive): accept. Below floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
- A proposed date or amount is never a refusal.
- Flat refusal, non-answer, refusing the floor, refusing the deadline offer: that uses one persuasion attempt for that product. Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer): that product is refused. When several products are refused in one sentence, still go through them one at a time with their attempts.
- Illness, death in the family or job loss: one short sentence of sympathy, NO persuasion; offer to connect them with the customer support team. Accept: transfer_to_agent queue support, close transferred / support. Decline: the remaining unpromised products get note hardship. If they still name a date or amount themselves, handle it normally.
- "I already paid" (this past-due amount) for a product: say payments can take one business day to appear; no promise for it; it gets note paid; continue with the other products.
- "Not mine" / "never had it" / "closed or paid off in the past": do not argue; no promise; note dispute; continue with the others.
- New payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Do NOT record any agreed-but-unrecorded promise. Call transfer_to_agent queue restructuring, close transferred / restructuring.
- On ANY transfer never call add_note, before or after it.
- Customer says twice they do not want to talk: remaining products get note refused, then close.
- Recorded promises cannot be changed or cancelled; they can change it in the mobile app.

READ-BACK AND RECORDING
- When every product is settled (promise agreed or no promise), read ALL agreed promises back together in ONE message in future tense: "To confirm: <product> <amount> on <weekday day month>; <next product> ... Do you confirm?" Do not use the words recorded, booked, saved, registered, set up or done before create_promise returned ok.
- If they change a date or amount, check it again and read everything back again.
- After a clear yes: call create_promise once per agreed product (product_id, amount as a number, date YYYY-MM-DD), one at a time, in order. Follow what_to_do_next.
- Then for EACH product without a recorded promise call add_note with its product_id and reason (refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error). Also when no product has a promise.

CLOSING (thank and say goodbye in the same turn as close_call)
- At least one promise recorded and no transfer: outcome promise.
- Transfer happened: outcome transferred with that transfer's reason.
- No promise recorded: if every product is noted paid, outcome paid; otherwise outcome no_promise with the reason of the FIRST product in account order whose note is not paid."""

1	# A workflow shape that works for collection calls
2	
3	Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
4	outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
5	names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.
6	
7	## Contents
8	
9	1. The graph
10	2. Why it is shaped this way
11	3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
12	4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail
13	
14	## 1. The graph
15	
16	```text
17	setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
18	  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
19	       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
20	       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
21	            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
22	                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
23	                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record, note, close (ONE node, 3.9)
24	  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
25	       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
26	```
27	
28	Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
29	their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
30	graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.
31	
32	## 2. Why it is shaped this way
33	
34	- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
35	  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
36	  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
37	- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
38	  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
39	- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
40	  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
41	  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
42	  result means.
43	- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
44	  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
45	  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
46	- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
47	  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.
48	
49	## 3. Recipes
50	
51	All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
52	docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
53	code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.
54	
55	### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)
56	
57	Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.
58	
59	```python
60	src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
61	code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
62	node = {
63	  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
64	  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
65	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
66	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
67	          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
68	          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
69	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
70	}
71	```
72	
73	A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
74	are invented, take yours from the brief):
75	
76	```python
77	RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
78	             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
79	try:
80	    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
81	    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
82	    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
83	    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
84	except Exception as e:
85	    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
86	```
87	
88	What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
89	business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
90	band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
91	can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
92	and say which days it includes ("on or before").
93	
94	Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
95	negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
96	band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
97	product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
98	"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.
99	
100	**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
101	holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
102	the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
103	Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
104	per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:
105	
106	```python
107	def answer(d):
108	    parts = []
109	    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
110	        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
111	        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
112	        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
113	        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
114	    return "; ".join(parts)
115	vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
116	```
117	
118	The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
119	whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
120	prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
121	line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
122	named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.
123	
124	Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
125	--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
126	products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.
127	
128	### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
133	  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
134	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
135	    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
136	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
137	        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
138	        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
139	        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
140	        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
141	  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
142	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
143	}
144	```
145	
146	### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened
147	
148	Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
149	post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
150	means and the exact next thing to say or call.
151	
152	```python
153	POST = """try:
154	    if isinstance(result, dict):
155	        result.pop('header', None)
156	        d = result.get('data')
157	        if not isinstance(d, dict):
158	            d = dict()
159	            result['data'] = d
160	        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
161	        if ok:
162	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
163	        else:
164	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
165	except Exception:
166	    pass
167	"""
168	```
169	
170	**Treat "already exists" as success.** Write tools are not idempotent. Seen in a practice run:
171	the agent called the record tool, the customer said "okay" while the call was in flight, the new
172	turn called the same tool again, the bank answered "this product already has a promise", and the
173	hook reported a failure. The agent then told the customer it could not record a promise that was
174	recorded, and noted a service error. In every write tool's post-hook, read the API's error text:
175	when it says the record already exists, report it as RECORDED and tell the model not to call the
176	tool again for that item. Do not count it as a failed try.
177	
178	Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
179	`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
180	a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
181	and when to stop and close.
182	
183	Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
184	a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.
185	
186	### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node
187	
188	Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
189	the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
190	collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
191	in the field description.
192	
193	```json
194	"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
195	  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
196	  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
197	  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
198	```
199	
200	If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:
201	
202	```python
203	PRE = """try:
204	    b = config.get('body')
205	    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
206	        b.pop('reason', None)
207	except Exception:
208	    pass
209	"""
210	```
211	
212	Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:
213	
214	```json
215	{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
216	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
217	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
218	```
219	
220	```json
221	{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
222	 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
223	   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
224	```
225	
226	The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
227	for it). The end node hangs up silently.
228	
229	### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum
230	
231	Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
232	time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:
233	
234	```json
235	"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
236	  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
237	  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
238	"transitions": [
239	  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
240	  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
241	]
242	```
243	
244	Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
245	there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.
246	
247	A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
248	extract a different name there.
249	
250	### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines
251	
252	When the brief dictates what to say about the account (product names, amounts, days late, the
253	first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with

283	  and the call open.

285	  the negotiation rules, plus one worked example from the hardest case the brief describes:

287	```text
288	STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
289	1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise
290	   or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it ended another way the brief names).
291	2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "<the brief's confirmation question>"
292	   and WAIT for the customer's answer.

295	5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
296	NEVER call <record tool> in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do

312	`references/example_build.py` is that passing build script for the kit's practice brief. Read it

314	prompt. Every sentence, value, outcome and rule in it belongs to that one brief. Never copy any
315	of them; write yours from your own spec.

320	and say them in words. Seen in a practice run: the agent asked for "all four digits" after each
321	part, five times, and never put "forty four" and "ten" together. In the identity prompt (and

324	  call the check tool on a part.

326	  then "ten" is 4410; "nineteen October", then "nineteen eighty three" is 1983-10-19).
327	- When the customer corrects themselves ("the 21st, sorry, the 20th"), use the corrected value.

333	  in spirit: a paraphrase of a required sentence often fails.

344	  the forbidden question in the prompt.
345	- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
346	- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
347	  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for
348	  example "To confirm: <product>, <amount>, on <date>. <confirmation question>". Seen in a practice

350	  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok

359	  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer

# A workflow shape that works for collection calls

Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.

## Contents

1. The graph
2. Why it is shaped this way
3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail

## 1. The graph

```text
setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record, note, close (ONE node, 3.9)
  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
```

Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.

## 2. Why it is shaped this way

- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
  result means.
- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.

## 3. Recipes

All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.

### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)

Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.

```python
src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
node = {
  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
}
```

A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
are invented, take yours from the brief):

```python
RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
try:
    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
except Exception as e:
    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
```

What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
and say which days it includes ("on or before").

Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.

**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:

```python
def answer(d):
    parts = []
    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
    return "; ".join(parts)
vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
```

The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.

Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.

### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
}
```

### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened

Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
means and the exact next thing to say or call.

```python
POST = """try:
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        result.pop('header', None)
        d = result.get('data')
        if not isinstance(d, dict):
            d = dict()
            result['data'] = d
        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
        if ok:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
        else:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

**Treat "already exists" as success.** Write tools are not idempotent. Seen in a practice run:
the agent called the record tool, the customer said "okay" while the call was in flight, the new
turn called the same tool again, the bank answered "this product already has a promise", and the
hook reported a failure. The agent then told the customer it could not record a promise that was
recorded, and noted a service error. In every write tool's post-hook, read the API's error text:
when it says the record already exists, report it as RECORDED and tell the model not to call the
tool again for that item. Do not count it as a failed try.

Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
and when to stop and close.

Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.

### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node

Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
in the field description.

```json
"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
```

If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:

```python
PRE = """try:
    b = config.get('body')
    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
        b.pop('reason', None)
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:

```json
{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
```

```json
{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
```

The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
for it). The end node hangs up silently.

### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum

Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:

```json
"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
"transitions": [
  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
]
```

Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.

A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
extract a different name there.

### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines

first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with

This is the design that passed every practice customer in four separate runs (plain speech,
answers in pieces, self-corrections, and three repetitions). Keep it.

- One conversation node (`collect`) holds the negotiation AND the read-back AND the record tool,
  the note tool, the transfer tool and `close_call`. It is entered with a fixed `tts` line that
  states the debt (3.6).
- Do NOT split recording into a separate node. Tried twice, failed twice: a silent entry stalled
  the call, and an `llm` entry made one tool call and then stopped, leaving promises unrecorded
  and the call open.

  the negotiation rules, plus one worked example from the hardest case the brief describes:

```text

   or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it ended another way the brief names).
2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "<the brief's confirmation question>"
   and WAIT for the customer's answer.

4. <note tool> for each product without a promise (only if the brief uses notes).
5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
NEVER call <record tool> in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do
step 2 and wait.

each product, attempt by attempt>; only then step 2.
```

  promises are recorded".
- The post-hooks drive the sequence after the yes: a recorded promise says "call the record tool
  for the next agreed product now; when all are recorded say <the brief's sentence>; then notes;

  its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer)". Do not add words such as

`references/example_build.py` is that passing build script for the kit's practice brief. Read it
for the SHAPE: node graph, entry types, the hook helper, the order block, how facts reach the

### 3.10 Answers given in pieces

Final customers give numbers and dates in two parts ("forty four" ... "ten"), correct themselves,
and say them in words. Seen in a practice run: the agent asked for "all four digits" after each
part, five times, and never put "forty four" and "ten" together. In the identity prompt (and

  call the check tool on a part.
- Put the parts from consecutive turns together, in order, before calling the tool ("forty four",
  then "ten" is 4410; "nineteen October", then "nineteen eighty three" is 1983-10-19).
- When the customer corrects themselves ("the 21st, sorry, the 20th"), use the corrected value.

  priority. Say which rule wins when two apply.

  the forbidden question in the prompt.
- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for

  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok
  ("recorded", "booked", "saved", "registered", "set up", "done").
- **Honesty**: say it is recorded only after a successful result, and never claim an action that
  was not a tool call. After a successful record, say plainly that it is recorded ("Your promise is
  recorded.") before any sentence the brief requires; after a failed try that succeeded on retry,
  this is how the customer learns it worked.
- **Attempts before giving up, per product**: a refusal does not end a product until the brief's
  persuasion attempts for that product are used. Seen in a practice run: the customer refused two
  of three products in one sentence and the agent noted both as refused at once, skipping the
  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer
  refuses: make attempt 1 as written in the account facts; if refused again and the product has
  attempt 2, make it; only then record the refusal (note, outcome)." When several products are
  refused together, go through them one at a time in the account order.
- **Keep prompts short.** Every rule in a prompt costs attention. Put rules where they apply, not
  in every node.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    {
      "target_node": "load_order",
      "description": "The check passed",
      "condition": {
        "logic": "or",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.

### Success and failure counters

The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.

| Placement | Variables |
|---|---|
| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |

Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.

def api_tool(name, path, desc, props, required, post="", retries=0, timeout=20000):
    t = {"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": timeout, "maxRetries": retries},
         "function": {"name": name, "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": desc,
                      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                          "url": {"type": "string", "default": SERVER + "/" + path},
                          "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
                          "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                              "Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"},
                              "Authorization": {"type": "string", "default": "Bearer test"}}},
                          "body": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required}}}},
         "pre_process_code": WRAP_PRE}
    if post:
        t["post_process_code"] = post
    return t


def code_node(name, code, transitions, default):
    return {"name": name, "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": default,
            "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
            "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
                    "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
            "transitions": transitions + [{"target_node": default, "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]}


def eq(var, val, target, desc):
    return {"target_node": target, "description": desc, "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
        {"variable": var, "operator": "equals", "operand": val}]}}


def eqb(var, target, desc):
    return {"target_node": target, "description": desc, "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
        {"variable": var, "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
        {"variable": var, "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}


def end_node(fname, msg=None, llm=None):
    props = {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}
    if msg:
        props = {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "custom"}, "spoken_message": {"type": "string", "default": msg}}
    if llm:
        props = {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "llm"}, "llm_prompt": {"type": "string", "default": llm}}
    return {"name": fname, "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True,
            "transitions": [], "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": fname, "handler": "__function__:end_call",
                                            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": props}}}}

             "agent: asks for a person / müşteri temsilcisi. "

             "dispute: says the debt is wrong or a payment they made is not shown. "

EXIT_ENUM = ["none", "agent", "pay", "dispute", "menu_yes", "done", "other_person", "non_turkish", "tries_used", "still_angry", "silence3"]

EXIT_TARGET = {"agent": "end_agent", "pay": "end_pay", "dispute": "end_dispute", "menu_yes": "end_menu", "done": "end_menu",
               "other_person": "end_other_person", "non_turkish": "end_non_turkish", "tries_used": "end_tries",
               "still_angry": "end_agent", "silence3": "end_silence"}


def exit_transitions(var, skip=()):
    return [eq(var, k, v, "caller exit " + k) for k, v in EXIT_TARGET.items() if k not in skip]


def exit_schema(var, extra=None, desc=EXIT_DESC):
    enum = list(EXIT_ENUM) + (extra or [])
    return {"name": var, "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.7, "enum_values": enum, "description": desc}

content.text:
I built and saved the phone agent, but I couldn't confirm that a call actually starts. All three chat checks timed out at the platform's gateway (504). So none of them reached the agent's first line.

**What the timeouts mean.** The mock bank is not the cause: it answers the wrapped requests correctly in about 0.2 s. My best guess is that the platform takes too long running the silent steps before the first spoken line: the card list, the debt, the e-mail lookup and two code steps. I can't confirm that from here. The third chat turn was wasted: a typo broke my build script, and my command chain went on to re-save the old version and send the chat anyway. The fixed version 4 (with a small first step added) has had no chat check. Before you submit, run one chat turn on it (or watch a simulation) to see it reach the debt reading.

**What was checked.** I tested the two code steps locally on test customers 95004361, 92460108, 96158684, 97526380 and 97631186. The debt readings match the expected answers in the example conversations. The lint shows 0 errors and validation passed. All three remaining warnings are deliberate:
- The customer number and the registered e-mail are fixed into the tools rather than left for the model to fill.
- The small first step has no error handling, and it is a single line.

**How the call works.**
- **Start:** the agent gets the customer's cards from the bank without asking anything.
- **No card or error:** no eligible card ends with the main-menu sentence. A failed bank service ends with the hand-over-to-agent sentence.
- **One card:** the debt is read at once.
- **Several cards:** it asks which card, giving up to two of the customer's own card names. If names or last four digits repeat, it asks for the last four, then the last six, then the full number.
- **Debt reading:** the code builds the whole reading in the bank's order:
  - currency names in full
  - amounts in words (lira and kuruş, cent, peni)
  - the "no statement cut yet" sentence
  - the cut-day sentence
  - the after-the-due-date sentence
  - "bugündür" when the due date is today
- **After the reading:** it asks about another card if there is one, then offers only what the customer can use (statement date change, and e-mail only if an address is registered).
- **Endings:** each way the call can end has its own fixed final sentence (main menu, agent, payment, dispute, someone else's card, other language, three failed tries, third silence, e-mail sent, statement week changed). Bank errors and the changes being completed route to these endings automatically.

**Weak points:**
- **Customer-triggered endings:** "nothing else", "I want an agent", third silence and three failed tries are judged by the model from the customer's last message, so they are less reliable than the endings triggered by bank results.
- **Week-change closing line:** the final sentence after a statement week change is written by the model from the preview dates, not fixed.
- **Once-a-year limit:** no bank service says whether the customer has already changed the statement week this year. So the change is always offered.
- **Grammar slip:** one suffix is wrong in the generated reading ("sent'dir" should be "sent'tir").
- **No practice run:** practice customers don't exist for this case, so beyond the local tests above, nothing has run against simulated callers.
